deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.

disable.description: The display name for this plugin instance. Max length is 255 characters.
disable.rationale: Toggles whether the plugin instance is disabled. Keeping security/observability-relevant plugins enabled (preventing them being silently disabled) preserves the controls they provide, so a policy can require it stay enabled.

display_name.description: The display name for this plugin instance. Max length is 255 characters.

location.description: Resource ID segment making up resource 'name'. It identifies the resource within its parent collection as described in https://google.aip.dev/122.
location.rationale: Determines the region/zone where the resource is created. Policy should restrict it to an approved-region whitelist for data residency; the allowed set is parameterised (a hardcoded example whitelist is acceptable).

plugin.description: Resource ID segment making up resource 'name'. It identifies the resource within its parent collection as described in https://google.aip.dev/122.

plugin_instance_id.description:
The ID to use for the plugin instance, which will become the final
component of the plugin instance's resource name. This field is optional.

* If provided, the same will be used. The service will throw an error if
the specified id is already used by another plugin instance in the plugin
resource.
* If not provided, a system generated id will be used.

This value should be 4-63 characters, and valid characters
are /a-z[0-9]-_/.

project.description: The ID of the project in which the resource belongs. If it is not provided, the provider project is used.
project.rationale: Not security relevant, but required for terraform json to operate.

actions.description: The action status for the plugin instance.

actions.action_id.description:
This should map to one of the action id specified
in actions_config in the plugin.

actions.schedule_cron_expression.description:
The schedule for this plugin instance action. This can only be set if the
plugin supports API_HUB_SCHEDULE_TRIGGER mode for this action.

actions.schedule_time_zone.description:
The time zone for the schedule cron expression. If not provided, UTC will
be used.

actions.curation_config.description: The curation information for this plugin instance.

actions.curation_config.custom_curation.description: Custom curation information for this plugin instance.

actions.curation_config.custom_curation..description:
The unique name of the curation resource. This will be the name of the
curation resource in the format:
'projects/{project}/locations/{location}/curations/{curation}'

auth_config.auth_type.description:
Possible values:
AUTH_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED
NO_AUTH
GOOGLE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT
USER_PASSWORD
API_KEY
OAUTH2_CLIENT_CREDENTIALS
auth_config.auth_type.rationale: Selects the authentication scheme the plugin instance uses. A policy should disallow weak/static auth (e.g. API key, basic user/password) and prefer managed identity, so the auth mechanism is enforced to a secure minimum.

auth_config.api_key_config.description: Config for authentication with API key.

auth_config.api_key_config.http_element_.description:
The location of the API key.
The default value is QUERY.
Possible values:
HTTP_ELEMENT_LOCATION_UNSPECIFIED
QUERY
HEADER
PATH
BODY
COOKIE
auth_config.api_key_config.http_element_.rationale: Not a secret, just a config.

auth_config.api_key_config.name.description:
The parameter name of the API key.
E.g. If the API request is "https://example.com/act?api_key=",
"api_key" would be the parameter name.
auth_config.api_key_config.name.rationale: Name of API key. Not security relevant.

auth_config.api_key_config.api_key.description: Secret provides a reference to entries in Secret Manager.

auth_config.api_key_config.api_key.secre.description:
The resource name of the secret version in the format,
format as: 'projects/*/secrets/*/versions/*'.

auth_config.google_service_account_confi.description: Config for Google service account authentication.

The service account to be used for authenticating request.

The 'iam.serviceAccounts.getAccessToken' permission should be granted on
this service account to the impersonator service account.
auth_config.google_service_account_confi.rationale: References the service account the plugin instance authenticates as. This is a pointer to an existing identity; we do not constrain which specific service account is referenced. The account's privileges are governed by IAM, not by this reference.

auth_config.oauth2_client_credentials_co.description:
Parameters to support Oauth 2.0 client credentials grant authentication.
See https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc6749#section-1.3.4 for more details.

auth_config.oauth2_client_credentials_co.rationale: OAuth2 client identifier for the plugin's credentials config. It is a non-secret identifier referencing an external client; the secret is held elsewhere. We do not constrain such identifiers, and a generic policy could not pin a team-specific client id.

auth_config.oauth2_client_credentials_co.description: Secret provides a reference to entries in Secret Manager.

The resource name of the secret version in the format,
format as: 'projects/*/secrets/*/versions/*'.

auth_config.user_password_config.description: Parameters to support Username and Password Authentication.

auth_config.user_password_config.usernam.rationale: Username for a user/password auth config. The username is not a secret and is a team-specific value; a generic policy cannot constrain it. The real control is disallowing basic user/password auth via auth_type rather than constraining the username.

auth_config.user_password_config.passwor.description: Secret provides a reference to entries in Secret Manager.

The resource name of the secret version in the format,
format as: 'projects/*/secrets/*/versions/*'.
